title: The payroll system: bought, failed, repaired, replaced
question: What do the district's own pages, its board agendas and the overseers say the payroll-system replacement cost, what went wrong, and what it cost to fix?
finding: The district switched on a new payroll system on 3 January 2022, declared a payroll state of emergency ten months later, and in February 2024 announced it would replace the system; the replacement started in July 2025. The repair was bought through a consulting contract first estimated at $2.8 million and then enlarged by up to $8,837,750. The Civil Grand Jury cited a $14 million figure from a newspaper headline; the implementation contract papers, saved in November 2026, give the contract's own amounts (screen schools_records.payroll-contract-prices). The State fiscal-crisis team wrote in 2024 that the errors' cost was something "the district is unable to estimate". The board was asked to act 17 times on contracts and resolutions for the two systems; 1 of those, extending the old system's supplier agreement, was on agendas after the new system started (2026-10-13).
how: A dated list assembled from three kinds of record: the titles of Board of Education agenda items that name the payroll system, its suppliers (SAP, Infosys, Labyrinth Solutions), the repair consultants (Alvarez & Marsal) or the replacement (Frontline, Red Rover); the district's own press releases and staff pages; and the reports of the Civil Grand Jury, the City Controller and the State fiscal-crisis team. Every quotation is checked against the document's text.
limits: The contracts themselves, with their prices, are on board item pages that could not be downloaded, so the cost of the original system, of the installer's four contract amendments and of the replacement is not known from these records; a records request for the item attachments would supply it. A failed system replacement is not evidence of wrongdoing by any supplier or employee. Agenda titles are proposals and do not show how the board voted.

Board asked to act: Agreement between the San Francisco Unified School District (SFUSD) and InfoSys Limited (Infosys). The agenda title gives no amount.
Board asked to act: Change order to the SAP Agreement. The agenda title gives no amount.
Board asked to act: Adding New SACs (Funding Source) to fund HCBM Project with Infosys Limited. The agenda title gives no amount.
Board asked to act: Infosys Ltd Contract, Second Amendment. The agenda title gives no amount.

rows.source: School district press release of 13 September 2022
rows.what: The new payroll and personnel system went live, replacing processes the district says had been in place for 17 years.
rows.quote: SFUSD transitioned to a new system for payroll, time and attendance, and other human resources' functions on Jan. 3, 2022

rows.what: Between 2022-03-22 and 2022-06-28 the board took up 4 agreements with employee unions about payroll errors and deferred pay.
Board asked to act: Third Amendment to Contract between the San Francisco Unified School District (SFUSD) and InfoSys Limited (Infosys). The agenda title gives no amount.

The district proposed hiring the consulting firm Alvarez & Marsal to clear the backlog of pay errors and stabilise the system: $805,000 for a first phase, with payroll and technology teams short of more than 15 staff.
rows.quote: The full engagement is estimated to be $2.8 million.

rows.what: Board asked to act: Agreement for Services with Alvarez and Marsal Public Sector Services, LLC (“A&M”) to Assess and Stabilize EMPowerSF. The agenda title gives no amount.
The superintendent declared a payroll state of emergency and set up a command centre of about 60 people drawn from district staff, the consultants and the contractor Infosys.
rows.quote: the problems with EMPowerSF are more substantial and complex than were originally known

rows.what: "Payroll State of Emergency Update" was a standing agenda item at 13 meetings from 2022-11-15 to 2023-12-12.
Board asked to act: Amendment to the Agreement for Services with Alvarez and Marsal Public Sector Services, LLC (“A&M”) to Assess and Stabilize EMPowerSF. The agenda title gives no amount.

The board unanimously enlarged the consultants' contract and doubled their staff in the command centre. The release says the engagement runs "through May 31, 2022", a date already past when it was issued; the source appears to mean 2023.
rows.quote: The amendment is for a contract increase not to exceed $8,837,750.00

rows.what: Board asked to act: Fourth Amendment to Contract between the San Francisco Unified School District (SFUSD) and Infosys Limited (Infosys). The agenda title gives no amount.
Board asked to act: Second Amendments to SAP Agreements for EMPowerSF. The agenda title gives no amount.
The grand jury found that pay errors, cancelled insurance and wrong deductions since January 2022 were hurting teacher hiring, and asked for a root-cause review of the purchase.
rows.quote: the unsuccessful purchase of a new payroll system

rows.source: San Francisco Civil Grand Jury, citing press reports
rows.what: The jury wrote that the cost of fixing the system had gone from $2.8 million to $8 million; its source list cites a San Francisco Chronicle headline of 15 September 2022 putting the purchase at $14 million. No district document on disk states the purchase price.
rows.quote: S.F. School District Paid $14 Million for a New Payroll System

rows.source: City Controller, reply to the grand jury
rows.what: The Controller declined to carry out the root-cause review the jury asked for, while saying a review after the system was stable was warranted.
rows.quote: jurisdiction, capacity, or technical knowledge of SAP payroll systems

rows.source: Board of Education, reply to the grand jury
rows.what: The school board accepted the jury's finding on payroll.
rows.quote: The District has long acknowledged that the payroll crisis is unacceptable

rows.what: The district announced it would replace the two-year-old system with a different one, Frontline Education's system for California school districts, paid for from money set aside in 2022. No price is given.
rows.quote: The target date for fully implementing this new system is July 2025.

rows.what: Board asked to act: 243-12Sp3 - Adoption of a New Enterprise Resource Planning System. The agenda title gives no amount.
Board asked to act: Approval of Contract with Red Rover HCM. The agenda title gives no amount.

rows.source: State Fiscal Crisis and Management Assistance Team
rows.what: The State team reported that the payroll system was not joined to the finance system, that errors had been pervasive for years and had not been traced, and that tax and pension reporting had been inaccurate and late.
rows.quote: this has caused significant errors in payroll and benefits, the impact of which the district is unable to estimate

rows.source: State Fiscal Crisis and Management Assistance Team
rows.what: Payroll staff told the State team that the accuracy of a pay run was not guaranteed and was checked with an exceptions report.
rows.quote: payroll warrants in the millions of dollars have been issued to individuals but that these large amounts have been caught before being paid to staff

rows.what: Board asked to act: SAP Futility Resolution and Cloud 3rd Amendment to Agreement (Order Form). The agenda title gives no amount.
Board asked to act: SAP Cloud 4th Amendment to Agreement (Order Form). The agenda title gives no amount.
Board asked to act: Contract to support Frontline and Red Rover implementation with Galaxy Solutions, Inc. The agenda title gives no amount.
The district reported that the replacement system, launched in July 2025, had paid about 4,500 employees with 78 corrections outside the normal pay run.
rows.quote: successfully processed payroll for nearly 9,000 employees since the launch of Frontline in July

rows.what: Board asked to act: Futility Resolution authorizing the District to contract with Red Rover Technologies, LLC. The agenda title gives no amount.

rows.source: State Fiscal Crisis and Management Assistance Team
rows.what: A year into the replacement system the State team found payroll staff able to change an employee's place on the salary scale, and staffing records not reconciled with budget and payroll.
rows.quote: changes to employees' direct deposit information are not independently reviewed after they are made

rows.what: Board asked to act: SAP Futility Resolution and Cloud 4th Amendment to Agreement (Order Form). The agenda title gives no amount.
